body:
Hi,
I took a look into this and I think the source of the issue is when TransportBulkAction goes to [process the request](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/149f4a1376819fc01107fcbe5ed9ad5278051bf3/server/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/action/bulk/TransportBulkAction.java#L680). The concrete write index is determined by `ia` (by calling `ia.getWriteIndex(...)`). 
When you run the request via the data stream name, `ia` is a DataStream and if the DataStream is a time series data stream specifically it uses the timestamp to [calculate](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/149f4a1376819fc01107fcbe5ed9ad5278051bf3/server/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/cluster/metadata/DataStream.java#L1115) the correct index . 
But when you run the request via the alias, `ia` is an Alias and it just uses whatever [index](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/149f4a1376819fc01107fcbe5ed9ad5278051bf3/server/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/cluster/metadata/IndexAbstraction.java#L254) is in its `writeIndex` field. For aliases to data streams, the `writeIndex` is the latest backing index.

To fix this I think the Alias class probably needs some way of knowing that it's a time series data stream, or perhaps a reference to the DataStream itself. 
From what I can tell the `referenceIndices` field in Alias contains all of the backing indices, so it might just be a matter of adding an extra `isTimeSeries` boolean and doing the timestamp logic on `referenceIndices`.

Hi @limotova, thank you for looking into this.

I agree with you, when we are approaching a data stream we use the `getWriteIndex(...)`, my initial thought is that the alias can check if it is a data stream alias and then it should delegate the write index resolution to the method `getWriteIndex(...)` of the data stream.

I do not think we need to add `isTimeSeries` boolean because we already have `dataStreamAlias` which I believe could be sufficient. Then what would be left is how to get hold of the data stream to delegate the method call. 

Do you agree?

issue.title: Fix write index resolution with aliases to TSDS's

issue.body:
Currently when you try to index a document to a TSDS via an alias the alias resolves to the latest backing index of the TSDS. This commit delegates finding the write index to the original data stream the alias points to.

Fixes #104189

body:
Yes I think it should be possible to give the alias access to the data stream and use only the `dataStreamAlias` boolean.
I made a draft PR https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/104440, just wanted to make sure this matches what you were thinking of before I add tests. I believe it fixes the issue though
It fetches the current write index (the latest backing index), gets its parent data stream, and then delegates `getWriteIndex(...)` to the parent data stream.

@limotova yes, that's exactly what I had in mind, I do not know off the top of my head if this is the most efficient way to retrieve the data stream (it might well be) but the idea is what I was thinking too.
Great, let me clean it up and add some tests then, I'll open a non-draft PR in a bit
